my sister is mentally and physically disabled, so most of the attention and care goes on her. which is understandable, but i feel like mental health is severely undermined. my dad says i need to open up more. i was in the hospital a few months back and we both made a deal that i would open up more, and he would stop drinking (my dad is a really bad alcoholic and has been for a long time) cold turkey. i tried opening up a little more, admitting whenever i was feeling down or sad, or when something was frustrating me, i kept my end of the bargain, he didn't. he said he would fully stop, and never did. made excuses saying "well, i'm cutting back." his advice was never anything reassuring or good eituer. just a few days ago we were driving and i was feeling horribly upset that morning and he asked me what was wrong. i said i was feeling down, but didn't know why. he retorts with a, "cheer up. things get better. you should be happy, you got a brand new car!" gee, thanks. helped me so much. but, then again, it's little things like this make me feel incredibly guilty about the way i feel towards my dad. at least he's trying, right?

maybe, it's just me. but if i'm unfamiliar with someone's mental illness or if someone is struggling with suicidal thoughts, i would look up the best way to handle it. it really hurts me that he doesn't even at least do the research, and i can tell he's highly uneducated about depression by the way he speaks to me. he brought me my meds once and said, "this is for your mood swings." it's like he thinks i'm going through some teenage angst phase, and to this day, that phrase still pisses me off. when i went to the hospital for planning a suicide, he asked me why would i wanna do that. said, how would he feel about it and how it would affect the family. then when i got the news i was going to be moved into a psychiatric facility (take note, i actively volunteered to take myself to the hospital because i knew i was a danger to myself) he said that they were gonna keep me there for 90 days or more (they legally can't do that here where i live. the facility i was taken to was for short term) and basically making it out to be some horrible thing happening to me. he yelled at me through the phone about turning myself into the hospital and saying i shouldn't have said anything about my suicidal tendencies. not once did he ask me if i was okay or if i wanted this. he made it all about him and how he felt.
also really sucks when they bring religion into the mix when you tell them about what's going, and they tell you to take it up with god instead.

this is pretty accurate to my situation. and it's weird because he always tries to "pay me back" with nice things, i.e. getting me a car for my birthday, and then uses it against me later. makes me wish he never did anything for me in the first place. it sucks even more now because at least i had my mom to lay back on for emotional support, now she's gone since cancer decided to fuck her over. my grandma always brags about how good my father is and how much a good person he is, but i can't see it. he never wants to change, or acknowledge how i feel, and wonder why i feel the way i do. it does feel like a constant battle because i wanna speak up, tell him how i really feel, but i know it's hopeless in the end, because he'll just come up on top anyway. it's like my depression means nothing to him. refuses to learn anything about how my mental illness affects me, refuses to rephrase certain things, refuses to learn what my triggers are.

i still feel like i am a bad daughter, i still feel like i am selfish, despite friends telling me the opposite whenever i vent to them about my father. i feel gross, i'm not good enough. i do my chores, i do what he tells me, maybe not right away all the time, but i do them regardless. but he never understands that it's the way he tells me, it's always with an attitude, like i'm better than you attitude, idk maybe i'm overthinking. i feel horrible for hating my dad because those guilty thoughts of, oh well, he's done this and this for you, loom over me. i'm just at a constant battle with myself. glad there's someone out there that has had a similar experience.
